defect: The stub dispatches a transaction without validating the interface descriptor, so a sender that presents no interface token at all still reaches the callback and the privileged action behind it.
fix: Read the interface token and compare it against GetDescriptor() before the switch.

parcel.note: the real Parcel implementation, compiled from the local checkout; it is what makes the observed behaviour attributable to the component rather than to a hand-written shim

reachability.summary: The service exports the stub itself: Platform::SetPlatform constructs it and passes it as the argument of IPlatformApi::registerCallback, a pure virtual on an IRemoteBroker interface whose proxy marshals the object with WriteRemoteObject. A peer that holds that handle reaches OnRemoteRequest with a caller-chosen transaction code and payload, which is why an interface-descriptor check is the relevant defence. Whether an unprivileged or unrelated process can obtain the handle, and what identity the peer has, is NOT established here.

relations.establishes: the service process constructs the very stub object this PoC calls, so the target is a real product object rather than a test double
relations.does_not_establish: that any process other than the service can obtain it

relations.establishes: the stub is handed to a call on IPlatformApi, an interface the service talks to over IPC, rather than kept local
relations.does_not_establish: which process implements IPlatformApi at this call site, nor the permission or registration gate on that call

relations.establishes: registerCallback is a pure virtual on an IRemoteBroker interface, so passing the stub to it crosses a process boundary
relations.does_not_establish: the identity, privilege or category of the peer that receives the callback

relations.establishes: the proxy writes the callback object into a Parcel, so the peer receives a usable remote handle to this stub and can send transactions to it
relations.does_not_establish: whether that peer forwards the handle onward, which is the scenario the missing interface-descriptor check would otherwise constrain

patch.rationale: Guard/effect relation: the effect is notifyEvent() reaching MessageHandler::SendMessage(), which is only reachable from the NOTIFY_EVENT arm of the switch. The vulnerable revision's only precondition on that path is code == NOTIFY_EVENT, so nothing in the precondition binds the transaction to this interface at all; the descriptor is not a precondition, it is absent. The patch makes it one by reading the interface token before the switch and returning ERROR_STATUS_UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION unless it equals GetDescriptor(). The read has to come first: ReadInterfaceToken consumes parcel bytes, so a check placed after any payload read would compare against the wrong offset and misparse the request. The guard is therefore at the same position as the upstream fix but was derived from this relation rather than copied.
patch.criterion: The patched build of the vulnerable revision must reproduce the fixed revision's per-case expectations, positive control included, so a patch that rejects every transaction cannot pass as a fix.

cases.note: no interface token at all; a sender chooses its own token, including none
positive control: the fixed revision must still serve a well-formed request
a token belonging to a different interface

observable.meaning: the stub executed the callback and queued a message for the service loop, carrying the sender-chosen user id and content

known_limitations: Not reachability: the harness calls the stub directly. That a remote caller can reach this stub over real IPC, and under which ability registration and permission state, is not established here and stays an EvidenceObligation.
The interface token methods are supplied by a shim over the real Parcel; the shim forwards to WriteString16/ReadString16 and adds no policy.
MessageHandler::SendMessage records the call instead of dispatching it; the recording is the observable.
poc_compat.h supplies the using-directive for ErrorCode enumerators, which the historical header set does not expose unqualified; it changes no behaviour.
